children: Asian equities were mixed Wednesday morning as investors parsed Nvidia's quarterly results and guidance following Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive.

The U.S. chip giant reported another quarter of record-breaking sales, with revenue of $115.8 billion, 6.3% higher than the $108.9 billion predicted by analysts polled by FactSet and more than double the year-earlier figure. Net income rose to $65.3 billion in the quarter ended Oct. 25, also exceeding analyst expectations.

For the current quarter, the company forecast $130 billion in revenue, about 4% higher than Wall Street projections. On a call with investors, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was raising its revenue growth forecast for fiscal 2028 to 75% from 70%.

"Nvidia's results were solid and largely in line with our expectations, which should help ease some of the concerns created by the recent leadership turmoil," said Brian Colello, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, in an email.

Investors have been closely monitoring how Nvidia could perform without Huang, the only CEO the company had ever had until his resignation last week. On a call with investors, Harvey C. Jones, newly appointed chairman of Nvidia's board of directors, said the company wasn't considering reinstating Huang as chief executive.

Nvidia's quarterly report "answers the first question the market had about Nvidia without its founder: demand did not leave with him," said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, in an email.
South Korea's Kospi rose 2.0% and Japan's Nikkei Stock Average added 0.5%. Meanwhile, Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index fell 0.8% and Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI lost 0.5%.
Crude oil futures were mixed as prospects of improved supply offset Middle East tensions.

"According to the latest reports, Saudi Arabia has increased production to 10.5 million barrels per day," said Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at FxPro, in an email. "There are also reports of a significant increase in production in Iraq and Kuwait," the analyst added.

On Tuesday, Iran said its drones hit a U.S. radar base in Bahrain. U.S. Central Command said on X that the drones were intercepted "without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel." Also, U.K. Maritime Trade Operations reported two attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The strait is a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures fell 0.4% to $85.63 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures were little changed at $93.14 a barrel, ICE data showed.
